1  -2-  NC: 2024:KHC:27304  CRL.P No. 4288 of 2024  THIS CRIMINAL PETITION IS FILED UNDER SECTION 439 CR.PC PRAYING TO ENLARGE THE PETITIONER ON BAIL CR.NO.09/2023 OF CHIKKABALLAPURA WOMEN POLICE STATION,
CHIKKABALLAPURA FOR AN OFFENCE PUNISHABLE UNDER SECTION 376(2)(N) OF IPC AND SECTIONS 5(L), 5(N), 5(J)(II), 6 OF POCSO ACT, 2012, NOW PENDING ON THE FILE OF HON'BLE ADDITIONAL DISTRICT AND SESSIONS JUDGE, FTSC-1 AT CHIKKABALLAPURA DISTRICT IN SPL.S.C.NO.26/2023.

THIS CRIMINAL PETITION COMING ON FOR ORDERS THIS DAY, THE COURT PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioner-accused is before this Court seeking grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. in Crime No.9 of 2023 of Chikkaballapura Women Police Station, pending in Spl.SC No.26 of 2023 on the file of the learned Additional District and Sessions Judge, FTSC-1 at Chikkaballapura District,
registered for the offences punishable under Section 376(n) of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC') and under Sections 5(L), 5(n), 5(J)(II), 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (for short 'the POCSO Act'), on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant Deepika.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
2. Heard Sri T A Basavaraju, learned counsel for the petitioner, Smt K P Yashodha, learned High Court Government NC: 2024:KHC:27304 Pleader for the respondent No.1 and Sri B Chandramouli,
learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Perused the materials on record.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Negative' for the following:
REASONS 4.
The petitioner being the sole accused is seeking grant of bail.
He was apprehended on 17.01.2023 and since then, he is in judicial custody.
The statement of the victim aged 16 years was recorded when she was admitted to the hospital and was diagnosed that she was pregnant.
It is stated that the petitioner has committed sexual assault on the innocent victim child, when she was still a minor.
The NC: 2024:KHC:27304 statement of the victim was recorded by the learned Magistrate under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., wherein, the victim has stated about the acts committed by the petitioner.
Further, it is stated that she became pregnant in view of the act committed by the petitioner.

It is Venkatesha K P vs State Of Karnataka By on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106921420/
2 pertinent to note that the learned Magistrate while recording the statement of victim has noted that the victim is not a normal girl and she is not in a position to state all the facts in detail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under such circumstances, it is clear that the victim is an innocent child and taking advantage of her an innocence, the petitioner said to have committed the offences.
However, it is for the prosecution to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
At present, there are sufficient materials to constitute the offence as alleged.

Even the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the respondent - accused have specifically stated that the petitioner has married the victim, as a result of which, she became pregnant and later delivered the child.
Considering the status of the victim there are strong prima facie materials to constitute the offence in question.
In view of all these facts ad circumstances, the petitioner is not entitled for grant of bail.

Accordingly, I answer the above point in the Negative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Criminal Petition is dismissed.
